tutorials.title: Find your way around
tutorials.summary: What is on the screen, and how your answers become a note for your care record.

steps.title: Answer what happened
steps.say: Gold Standard Notes writes a complete, person-centred care note from what actually happened on your shift. There is no account and no internet connection, and nothing you type leaves the device.

steps.title: Start with the person
steps.say: At the top is the person you are writing about. Their profile is saved on this tablet, so you only set it up once.

steps.title: Five short steps
steps.say: Below that, five steps follow the order of a good care record: what was offered, their choice, the support you gave, what you observed, and how it ended.

steps.title: The note writes itself
steps.say: On the right, the note builds as you answer. It only ever says what you recorded, never anything you did not.

steps.title: Smart Assist checks it
steps.say: Underneath, Smart Assist points out anything missing or inconsistent, and always tells you why.

steps.title: Copy it into Nourish
steps.say: When the note is complete, tick the confirmation and copy it. Then paste it into the daily note box in Nourish.

tutorials.title: Add a person
tutorials.summary: Set up someone's profile once, so the app asks the right questions about them.

steps.title: Add a person
steps.say: Tap Add person. Type their initials only, never a full name, and choose their pronouns.

steps.title: How they communicate
steps.say: Tick how they usually communicate. When you write a note, these are marked as their usual methods.

steps.title: Needs and risks
steps.say: Tick any standing needs or risks, such as a choking risk. They decide which questions you are asked. On their own, they never write anything into a note.

steps.title: More about them
steps.say: Open More about this person to add details, like a prescribed diet texture or a daily fluid target.

steps.title: A reminder at the top
steps.say: Their profile now shows as a reminder at the top of the page, every time you write about them.

tutorials.title: Write a personal care note
tutorials.summary: Record a morning routine, from the offer to the outcome, and copy the finished note.

steps.title: Choose the interaction
steps.say: Choose the type of interaction, which one it was, and the time.

steps.title: What was offered
steps.say: Record what was offered. Offering two real options is what shows they had a choice.

steps.title: How you communicated
steps.say: Tick how you communicated with them this time. Their usual methods are one tap away.

steps.title: Their choice and consent
steps.say: Record what they chose, how they let you know, and their consent.

steps.title: Support and independence
steps.say: In step three, tick each task and choose how much help was needed. What they did for themselves is written first.

steps.title: What you observed
steps.say: In step four, record only what you saw. Here, the door was closed for privacy, and nothing new was seen on their skin.

steps.title: How it ended
steps.say: Then choose how it ended for them.

steps.title: Confirm and copy
steps.say: Read the note, tick the confirmation, and copy it. It pastes into Nourish as one block of text.

tutorials.title: Questions from the profile
tutorials.summary: How someone's needs bring up the right questions, and how a safety event is recorded.

steps.title: A meal for someone at risk
steps.say: This person's profile records a choking risk. When you record their lunch, questions appear at the top of step four.

steps.title: Why am I seeing this?
steps.say: Each group says why it is there. Nothing goes into the note until you answer.

steps.title: Answer what you know
steps.say: Answer only what you know. Each answer adds exactly one sentence to the note, and a question you leave alone adds nothing.

steps.title: A safety event
steps.say: If you record that choking was observed, Smart Assist marks it as critical, and offers a factual line for the handover. It never says anyone was told, unless you record that yourself.

steps.title: Describe it in your own words
steps.say: The note cannot be copied until you describe what happened, in your own words.

tutorials.title: When answers don't agree
tutorials.summary: Smart Assist spots answers that cannot both be true, and words that judge rather than describe.

steps.title: Two answers that disagree
steps.say: If two answers cannot both be true, Smart Assist flags them for review. Here, the overall support says fully independent, but the wash was done by staff.

steps.title: See the reason
steps.say: Open Why am I seeing this, to see the reason.

steps.title: Correct or explain
steps.say: Correct whichever answer is wrong, or tap Explain and say what happened. Your explanation goes into the note word for word, and copying unlocks.

steps.title: Describe, don't label
steps.say: Smart Assist also questions vague or judgemental words, like fine, or difficult. It never changes what you typed. It asks what you actually saw.

tutorials.title: Activities and college
tutorials.summary: Community activities, the journey there, and college sessions from a weekly timetable.

steps.title: A community activity
steps.say: For activities, choose the activity. For someone with a visual impairment, a walk in the community brings up questions about orientation.

steps.title: The journey
steps.say: Tick Travelling there to record the journey. Safety choices for that kind of journey, like waiting together at the stop, then appear.

steps.title: A weekly timetable
steps.say: For college, add their weekly sessions to their profile, just once.

steps.title: College fills itself in
steps.say: Then choose College. Today's course and times fill in from the timetable.

steps.title: What they did and gained
steps.say: Tick the particular things they did, like washing their hands before handling food. Then record the skills they practised, and how they got on with others. That is where a college note shows its value.

tutorials.title: Reword, length and sources
tutorials.summary: Fresh wording every time, the right length, and where each sentence came from.

steps.title: Fresh wording
steps.say: Reword it gives the same note in fresh wording. It checks that every fact, number and time stays exactly the same.

steps.title: Choose a length
steps.say: Short, Gold standard and Full detail change how much is said. If a length leaves something out, the note tells you, and Include everything puts it back.

steps.title: Where each sentence came from
steps.say: Developer view, at the foot of the page, shows which answer each sentence came from. It is there for managers who want to check.

tutorials.title: Settings, history and backups
tutorials.summary: Set up your service, notice changes in someone's usual pattern, and keep a backup.

steps.title: Your service's settings
steps.say: Settings and data lets your service use its own wording. Here, the care-record system is set to Nourish.

steps.title: Keep a history
steps.say: Switch on Keep structured history, and each copied note saves what it observed: amounts, levels and choices, never the written note.

steps.title: Changes in someone's pattern
steps.say: Over time, Recent pattern shows what is usual for each person, and Smart Assist points out a change, like three low meals in a row. It never suggests a diagnosis.

steps.title: Keep a backup
steps.say: Everything stays on this device, so download a backup regularly. Restore it on another tablet to copy the same setup.
